dfc-3v3.about:
Welcome to the Dead Fools Club. The battlefield is a toy diorama on your real table, and your fighter is a little fool with a big gun.

• Press PLAY: a quick online match for up to 6 players.
• Squads: invite friends, play on one team and go into a match together.
• Four survivors of the club's first secret game: BURNS — shotgun, grenades over walls, heals the squad; SMITH — piercing sniper rifle and homing missiles; IRON — flamethrower and bazooka; BEANS — burst rifle, bombs, mines and smoke.
• Twelve boards: forest, sandstorm canyon, sliding ice, a turret fortress, a colosseum, the big Showdown arena, a plywood Killhouse and two steel mazes where bullets ricochet off the walls up to ten times.
• Fog of war on the night boards: you see only what your own lamp lights.
• Storm the enemy base, race to 20 frags, or be the last team standing while the zone closes in.
• Come back every day: a pink robe, a hot dog costume and red bullets for days in a row.
• Clan tags, a friends panel, friends and world leaderboards.
• A live announcer in your language — 12 languages.
• Mixed reality: lean over the board, grab it and turn it, play seated or standing.

Buy the game and you are in the club: your own fighter — endless clothes, hairstyles and accessories — and your own rooms with any board and mode, from the very first match.
Requires an internet connection.

wet-bottom.about:
Wet Bottom is the sea battle you played on paper, projected as a hologram into your room.

A tray of glowing contour lines becomes the sea. Your fleet rides the swell; on your turn the projector flickers over to the enemy's waters — another seabed, ships you cannot see until you sink them.

AIM ANY WAY YOU LIKE
• Turn two ship's wheels and slam the big red button
• Look at a cell, or drop a pointer arc on it
• Tap it on a small tablet beside the console
• Write it in the air with a pinch — "D6"
• Or hold the radio key and say it: "delta six, fire!" (recognised on the headset)

TWO WAYS TO PLAY
• Turn by turn: a hit fires again
• Countdown salvo: ten shots your first turn, nine the next… down to one

PLANES, SUBMARINES, AA GUNS
Earn coins, buy them from the rack at your elbow. Fly a bomber down two columns, send a submarine under the enemy's fleet and aim its torpedo, keep AA guns ready for the raids that come back at you.

CLIMB THE RANKS
From Cabin Boy to Admiral: each rank a sharper gunner.

PLAY A FRIEND ONLINE
Invite a friend from Meta Horizon or share a 4-digit room code, then battle one-on-one. Climb the world and friends Victories leaderboards.

MADE FOR MIXED REALITY
Play over your real room, in darkness or under a dusk sky. Lay the sea flat, tilt it to 45° or stand it up like a wall — the console stays at your hands. Drag the whole field wherever it suits you.

Hand tracking first; Touch controllers work too. A navigator calls the battle in English or Russian.

valxr.about:
VALXR puts a whole survivor roguelite on your table. A tiny hero runs across a diorama world, the ghosts keep coming, and every level-up makes you a little more absurd: faster, bouncier, tougher, bloodthirstier — until the table is nothing but bullets.

SURVIVE TEN MINUTES
• Waves of ghosts, bats, brutes, spitters, chargers, bombers and swarms
• Champions at 3:00 and 6:00, a boss portal at 7:00 — call the boss when you are ready
• Clear the stage to unlock the next one

BUILD A RIDICULOUS RUN
• Weapons that level up and overload at level 8: guns, swords, orbiting stones, fire and frost trails, mines, lightning
• Mutations: poison, burning, ice and shock rounds
• Tomes, rare offers, chests with items, shrines, crates and booster drops

EIGHT STAGES
Yard, Moon (half gravity!), Canyon, Sweet Shop, Toy Box, Arcade, Picnic and Board Game — each with its own crowd and hazards.

SEVEN HEROES
KIDDO, TIN CAN, FISHSTICK and the Dead Fools Club gang — BURNS, SMITH, IRON and BEANS with their own guns and skills.

KEEP COMING BACK
Spend silver in the Workshop, finish quests, unlock heroes and climb three difficulty tiers.

Made for mixed reality: the arena sits on your real table, you play with Touch controllers, seated or standing.

trrrack.about:
**STEERING THAT MAKES YOU GRIN.** Your starfighter goes exactly where you point it. Thread the gap, kiss the apex, carve a corner on the air brakes or sideshift a lane.

**120 HZ. EVERYTHING ANSWERS.** On Quest 3 every flick of the stick and every hit comes back the moment it happens.

**SPEED YOU FEEL.** Boost pads kick you forward, the road drops into jumps and climbs into loops under burning sunsets and starlit skies.

**SIMPLE AT FIRST SIGHT. DEEP IN EVERY LAP.** One energy bar is your turbo and your hull. Burn it or save it. Fire now or wait for the straight. Mines or shield.

**A FIELD THAT FIGHTS BACK.** Seven rivals, missiles, lightning and mines on every circuit. Blast their mines off the road. A commentator calls every lap, pass and hit.

**YOUR GARAGE, YOUR ROOM.** Five starfighters, 37 liveries. Switch on mixed reality and the track runs through your room.

**YOU AGAINST YOU.** Race the ghost of your best lap and climb the leaderboards with friends.

Match-3 you can actually touch. The board floats in your real room in mixed reality, and you play with your bare hands. Reach out, touch a cube, slide it, watch three pop. No controllers. Just your fingers.
Feel weird in the best way. Play with four fingers. Play with giant hands. Slip magic rings onto your finger and blast through webs, ice and chains. Your hands have never felt this strange, or this fun.
150 beautiful levels. Every board is a little show, and the mechanics keep surprising you. Lost? Replay right away. No lives, no waiting, no "come back in 30 minutes".
Feed the chest. Get paid in burps. Chester is a treasure chest with teeth, one eye and zero manners. Grow fruit and craft on your farm, feed him, and he burps gold right back at you. Hungry yourself? Bring the fruit to your mouth, eat it, and burp coins too.
Your soundtrack, your rules. Load your own music and play to it, turn on YouTube, put on lofi, or listen to the full audiobook of Homer's Odyssey while you match.
Make it yours. Grab the board with your fist to move or resize it. Wear cartoon gloves or astronaut hands. Leave your room for a quiet valley, a sunset dome or an orbit above the Moon.
Mixed reality, safe and sound. You see everyone around you. Please don't step on your pets.
Try it free. Play the first levels before you buy. Built for hand tracking on Quest 3 and 3S; controllers work too.

astrowitch.about:
Psst… yes, you. Come closer.

Lupita has been waiting for you in her candle-lit parlour. Sit at her table and simply talk: she listens, answers in her own voice and leads every reading.

WHAT SHE READS FOR YOU
• Your Sign — a portrait of your zodiac sign from your birth date.
• Your Ascendant — tell her when and where you were born; she sets the date on her brass astrolabe and calculates your rising sign from the real sky of that minute.
• Your Year and Your Month — big transits, eclipses, retrogrades, golden and careful days, each explained in plain words.
• Tarot — shuffle the deck and draw three cards with your own hands.
• I Ching — toss the coins six times and watch your hexagram burn in the air.

THE REAL SKY
Planet positions are computed on your headset with astronomical formulas; a glowing chart of your stars rises above the table.

SHE REMEMBERS YOU
Lupita asks your name and keeps it, your birth data and your past readings encrypted on your headset only.

FREE TO SIT DOWN
Your sign, a short reading of your year and your rising sign, and a weekly tarot and I Ching reading are free. The full Year Book, monthly forecasts, the full birth chart and extra time with Lupita are optional purchases, always shown with their price on a wax seal you touch only if you want it.

GOOD TO KNOW
AstroWitch is an entertainment experience. Lupita's voice and answers are generated by AI (Google Gemini) and are not advice of any kind. Needs internet and a microphone. English. 18+.

dfc-manager.about:
Dead Fools Club: Manager is a round-based tactics game for your tabletop. You don't shoot — you lead.

BUY. Each fighter stands over his own console. Press the keys with your fingers or a controller: guns from his specialist's arsenal, armour, a one-shot gadget. One squad bank pays for everything, so every round is a choice — a full buy, a cheap round to save up, or one sniper rifle for the right man.

ORDER. Attack site A or B, or split your defence and give each fighter a role: anchor, patrol, flank, lurker or push. Change the call live while the round plays out.

WATCH. Five against five on fifteen boards, by day or by the light of their torches at night. The fighters see only what is in front of them, call out over the radio, trade kills, take cover and roll away from grenades. Plant the bomb, or defuse it before it blows.

BUILD. Wounds carry over between rounds. Heal your veterans and keep their gear, sell a fighter and hire another specialist for the next map, which you see before you buy.

PLAY. Against a bot opponent, or online, one on one, against another manager.

Free. No ads, nothing for sale in battle — if you enjoy it, you can support the servers after a match.
